The problem

Bad routing does not fail loudly. It leaks, in ways that never show up on a single invoice.

Three in every ten kilometres are driven with nothing on board.

Hollow trucks run empty.

Up to one in five deliveries fails on the first attempt.

Hollow parcels failed. Grey ones may.

More than half of UK operators still plan routes by hand.

Grid screens are spreadsheets.

Nearly nineteen weeks of every working year, lost to manual planning in a 10 driver operation.

One square per working day.

Empty running: Department for Transport road freight statistics. Other figures are estimates.

What it is

The map is the easy part. The hard part is who is working, what they are qualified for, and the order that arrives at 10am. Syncnox plans all of it together.

MCP

Your AI agents can run the plan too. Syncnox speaks MCP, the open standard AI assistants use to call tools.

What that means for you: the assistant your team already uses can add a job, re-plan the day and read an ETA. It works inside the limits you set, the same as the Syncnox agent.

  • 01Add jobsAddress, job type and date. The job lands on the plan.

    115 QUESTIONS

    Syncnox is always-on AI route optimization for field operations. One AI agent plans every route, crew and job, then watches the day and adapts the moment something changes.

    Route optimization, workforce scheduling, jobs, fleet tracking, asset tracking and analytics run on one platform, on one map and one record.

    Syncnox doesn’t stop at the morning plan. One AI agent monitors routes, jobs and schedules throughout the day, detects changes such as delays, cancellations and urgent jobs, and re-plans the open work automatically or with your approval.

    Route planning puts stops in an order. Route optimization solves the whole day at once: time windows, capacity, skills, shifts, priorities, depots and access rules together.

    Syncnox builds routes the way your operation actually runs, not shortest path on a map, and keeps re-optimizing as the day changes.

    Most route planners stop at the morning plan, and re-planning is usually a manual re-run. Syncnox keeps one agent on every route, crew and job, re-optimizes only the open work when something changes, and tracks vehicles and equipment on the same map.

    Telematics platforms track vehicles, and route optimization is usually basic or an add-on. In Syncnox, tracking, maintenance, fuel and geofencing feed the plan, so when a vehicle is unavailable the agent redistributes its work automatically.

    Field service management is one of the modules: scheduling, dispatch and job updates for every crew. It runs on the same platform as route optimization, GPS vehicle tracking, asset tracking, maintenance and inspections.

    Turn on what your operation needs. Nothing to reconcile between tools.

    Dynamic route optimization re-plans routes while the day is running, not only before it starts. In Syncnox the agent monitors progress, detects delays, cancellations and urgent jobs, and re-optimizes only the open work.

    Software that plans and runs the work done away from the office: routes, crews, jobs, vehicles and equipment. Syncnox covers route optimization, re-planning, alerts, workforce scheduling, jobs and integrations on one platform, connected by one agent.

    An AI dispatcher makes or recommends dispatch decisions as the day changes. In Syncnox that is the always-on agent: it plans, monitors, detects, re-plans and notifies, within the autonomy level you set.

    Routing is NP-hard, so no solver finds a provably perfect plan for a real day in the time dispatch has. What matters is how close it gets, how fast, and that it never proposes a plan you can’t run.

    Yes. Urgent orders are inserted mid-shift, and urgent jobs are offered to the nearest qualified technician.

    Yes. Syncnox plans the routes, assigns the jobs and dispatches drivers and technicians. In Autonomous mode the agent plans, re-plans and dispatches end to end. In Manual mode it recommends and your dispatchers apply each change in one click.

    Yes. Skills and certifications are built into every plan, so only qualified technicians and drivers get the job. Urgent jobs are offered to the nearest qualified technician.

    Yes. When a driver runs late, calls out or a vehicle becomes unavailable, the agent moves the affected stops to whoever has capacity and notifies the drivers. Depending on your autonomy level it applies the change or asks for approval first.

    A call-out redistributes their work to whoever has capacity. Routes and rosters are planned together, so the new assignments still respect skills, shifts and hours.

    Yes. Load limits are part of every plan. For fuel and energy runs, capacity and load compatibility are planned per run, and for waste rounds, tip runs are planned before the truck is full.

    Yes. Urgent jobs are offered to the nearest qualified technician, with the right tools and vehicle.

    Yes. Dispatch matches the technician, tools and vehicle to the job. In healthcare transport, vehicles and crews are matched to the patient, such as wheelchair access.

    Yes. Pickup and delivery are both job types, and pickup before delivery can be planned on the same vehicle.
